blueprint.title: Bali, Indonesia — Ubud and Jimbaran Leisure Journey
blueprint.summary: Use two bases and only one hotel change: four nights at Bisma Eight Hotel in Ubud (recommended, not booked) from October 5–9, followed by three nights at Jimbaran Puri, A Belmond Hotel (recommended, not booked) from October 9–12. Bisma Eight is preferred over the more secluded Maya Ubud because its central location reduces friction for the Monkey Forest, Campuhan Ridge, museums, textiles, and dining; a private driver handles the north-Ubud loop. Jimbaran provides a restful beachfront finish, practical access to Uluwatu, and a shorter departure-day route to DPS. October 3–4 are treated as pre-departure and long-haul travel days because the confirmed local arrival is October 5. The pace alternates substantial cultural days with lower-energy coastal time, protects arrival and departure, and avoids motorcycles. All lodging and activity reservations remain unbooked unless subsequently confirmed.

places.name: Tirta Empul Temple

guideDisplay.cardSummary: Living Balinese Hindu water temple centered on sacred springs and purification pools.
guideDisplay.footerNote: This remains an active place of worship.

places.whyWorthIt: The complex centers on natural springs, historic temple architecture, worship, and the living melukat purification tradition.
places.plan: Visit with a driver and pair it with Tegallalang. Observe worship respectfully; participate in purification only after learning the correct sequence and restrictions from an authorized local guide or temple staff.
places.tip: Wear temple-appropriate clothing and use the required sarong. Two waterspouts are reserved for rites associated with the dead and must not be used by ordinary bathers.

detailSections.title: Sacred use

localFoods.title: Babi guling
localFoods.description: Balinese ceremonial-style roast pork seasoned with an aromatic spice paste.
localFoods.context: Seek it from an established specialist if the travelers eat pork; it is best treated as a local-food theme rather than a default scheduled meal.

localFoods.title: Pepes-style seafood
localFoods.description: Fish or seafood seasoned with spices, wrapped in banana leaf, and steamed or grilled.
localFoods.context: Especially relevant around Jimbaran, where seafood and fishing-village traditions shape local menus.

localFoods.title: Regional Indonesian cooking
localFoods.description: A broader food theme spanning Balinese, Javanese, Sumatran, Sulawesian, and other Indonesian traditions.
localFoods.context: Useful for balancing specifically Balinese meals with an introduction to the archipelago’s wider food culture.

localProducts.title: Balinese painting
localProducts.description: Traditional and modern Balinese painting includes distinct Ubud-area schools, techniques, and historical periods.
localProducts.context: Museum visits provide context before considering any art purchase; do not treat museum collections as retail inventory.

localProducts.title: Indonesian handwoven textiles
localProducts.description: Textiles whose fibers, dyes, motifs, maker communities, and island origins form part of the object rather than serving as generic souvenirs.
localProducts.context: Threads of Life is a concrete place to browse these textiles and learn how natural dyes and weaving traditions relate to their communities of origin.

experienceThemes.title: Subak landscapes
experienceThemes.description: Bali’s cooperative irrigation tradition connects water management, agriculture, community, and religious practice.
experienceThemes.context: Tegallalang is the most accessible researched landscape expression of this theme from an Ubud base.

experienceThemes.title: Living temple etiquette
experienceThemes.description: Bali’s temples are active places of worship whose visitor value depends on respectful dress and behavior.
experienceThemes.context: At Tirta Empul, ritual participation requires more care than ordinary sightseeing.

experienceThemes.title: Balinese foodways
experienceThemes.description: Markets, local ingredients, ceremonial dishes, and hands-on cooking reveal how food connects to family and village life.
experienceThemes.context: A cooking class offers more context than adding multiple restaurant meals to the formal itinerary.

experienceThemes.title: Balinese visual and performance arts
experienceThemes.description: Compare painting traditions, masks, puppetry, textiles, and dance as distinct artistic practices rather than treating Ubud culture as one interchangeable category.
experienceThemes.context: The batch adds museum, mask-and-puppet, and textile choices that complement the scheduled Uluwatu Kecak performance and existing Ubud museums.

experienceThemes.title: Pakerisan Valley archaeology
experienceThemes.description: Rock-cut monuments, sacred river landscapes, and hermitage spaces provide historical depth beyond the active water-temple experience at Tirta Empul.
experienceThemes.context: Gunung Kawi is the concrete addable choice, but its stairs and visit duration make it a replacement-level decision rather than casual filler.

experienceThemes.title: Uluwatu coast without a surf commitment
experienceThemes.description: Cliff approaches, beach time, and expert surf scenery can be appreciated without scheduling a surf lesson or entering difficult breaks.
experienceThemes.context: Thomas and Suluban are concrete coastal choices; water entry remains conditional on current official and local safety information.

alternatives.title: ARMA indoor alternative
alternatives.summary: Use ARMA instead of Campuhan Ridge Walk if outdoor conditions are poor; do not add it on top of the full plan.

alternatives.title: Gunung Kawi archaeology alternative
alternatives.summary: For travelers prioritizing archaeology and able to manage substantial stairs, replace Tegallalang with Gunung Kawi; do not compress all three major sites into one day.

alternatives.title: Simple central-Ubud dinner
alternatives.summary: If Locavore NXT is not booked, dine near the hotel and use the extra time to pack and rest.

alternatives.title: Jimbaran Bay leisure day
alternatives.summary: If the class is unavailable, use the morning and early afternoon for meaningful beachfront rest and arrange a locally guided food-focused meal rather than inserting a distant attraction.

alternatives.title: Kayu Mama wellness replacement
alternatives.summary: If coastal conditions make Thomas Beach unsuitable, use a pre-booked spa or pool-access product before proceeding to Uluwatu Temple.

researchGrounding: The supplied ResearchSet contains 24 concrete places across both proposed bases, including four accommodation candidates and sufficiently varied cultural, landscape, food, beach, wellness, and weather-backup options. No supplemental research was needed to construct complete, geographically coherent days.

The base strategy uses the researched accommodation windows directly: Ubud from October 5–9 and Jimbaran from October 9–12. Bisma Eight was selected for walkable central-Ubud access; Jimbaran Puri was selected for its bay setting and practical relationship to DPS.

Ubud planning is grounded in official or identified sources for Sacred Monkey Forest Sanctuary, Museum Puri Lukisan, ARMA, Tegallalang Rice Terrace, Tirta Empul, Hujan Locale, and Locavore NXT, plus supplied research for Campuhan Ridge and Threads of Life.

The north-Ubud day deliberately excludes Gunung Kawi from the primary plan because its stairs and 150-minute visit would compress Tegallalang and Tirta Empul. It remains a replacement for Tegallalang, not an add-on.

South-Bali planning is grounded in the supplied Uluwatu Temple and Kecak research, Jala Cooking Academy, Cuca, Thomas Beach, Kayu Mama, official coastal-safety guidance, and the two Jimbaran accommodation candidates.

Neka Art Museum, Setia Darma House of Masks and Puppets, and Suluban Beach are intentionally not scheduled: Neka would repeat the selected art museums, Setia Darma would add a separate south-of-Ubud vehicle excursion, and Suluban’s stairs and surf-access character add less relaxed value than Thomas Beach for this party.

places.name: Sacred Monkey Forest Sanctuary

guideDisplay.cardSummary: Temple forest, mature trees, and semi-wild long-tailed macaques in central Ubud.
guideDisplay.footerNote: Follow the sanctuary’s macaque-safety rules.

places.visitRole: core Ubud nature and culture stop
places.whyWorthIt: The sanctuary combines a forest landscape, Balinese temple precincts, conservation work, and close observation of macaques.
places.plan: Use a morning or later-afternoon slot and follow the official rules: do not touch or feed monkeys, secure loose belongings, and avoid direct confrontation.
places.tip: Carry no visible food and keep sunglasses, phones, and small loose items secured.

detailSections.title: What stands out
detailSections.body: The official sanctuary describes more than 1,000 macaques, 186 tree species, temple areas, and conservation facilities.

detailSections.title: Safety
detailSections.body: The macaques are semi-wild rather than pets.
items: Do not retrieve an item directly from a monkey.

images.alt: Long-tailed macaque in the Sacred Monkey Forest Sanctuary

supports: The site contains macaques, a forest with 186 tree species, and temple areas.

places.name: Museum Puri Lukisan

guideDisplay.cardSummary: Historic Ubud museum focused on Balinese painting and woodcarving.

places.whyWorthIt: The museum provides historical context for modern Balinese painting and woodcarving in a garden setting near Ubud Palace.
places.plan: Pair it with a compact central-Ubud walk rather than a separate driver excursion.
places.tip: It is about 300 metres west of Ubud Palace according to the museum.

detailSections.title: Best use
detailSections.body: Use this as an indoor cultural anchor when outdoor conditions are poor or when the group wants a lower-energy day.

supports: The museum states it is about 300 metres west of Ubud Palace.
Opening hours are 09:00–18:00 daily.
The official page publishes an adult entrance fee, establishing paid admission.

schedulingEligibility.reason: Map-ready indoor attraction in central Ubud, useful during heat or rain.

supports: The museum publishes its Ubud address and daily hours.

places.name: Agung Rai Museum of Art

guideDisplay.cardSummary: Balinese and Indonesian art collections set within a landscaped cultural complex.
guideDisplay.footerNote: Check the current program directly if seeking a performance or workshop.

places.whyWorthIt: ARMA combines Balinese and Indonesian paintings with gardens and an active cultural center.
places.plan: Choose it instead of, rather than in addition to, Museum Puri Lukisan when pacing calls for one substantial museum.
places.tip: Performance and workshop programming is separate from ordinary museum access and should be checked for the chosen date.

detailSections.title: Scope
detailSections.body: The permanent collection includes Balinese, Indonesian, and foreign artists, while the wider complex supports performances and workshops.

images.alt: Balinese-style buildings and tropical grounds at the Agung Rai Museum of Art

supports: ARMA describes its permanent collection, exhibitions, performing arts, and workshops.

schedulingEligibility.reason: Map-ready Ubud museum suitable as an indoor or lower-energy alternative.

supports: ARMA identifies itself as an Ubud museum and center for visual and performing arts.

places.name: Campuhan Ridge Walk

guideDisplay.cardSummary: Paved ridge path between two river valleys near central Ubud.
guideDisplay.footerNote: The ridge has little shade.

places.whyWorthIt: The ridge gives open valley views within walking distance of central Ubud.
places.plan: Start early, navigate to Pura Gunung Lebah rather than a generic trail pin, and choose an out-and-back distance that matches the group’s energy.
places.tip: Bring water and sun protection; the ridge section is exposed.

detailSections.title: Route character
detailSections.body: The cited guide describes a paved ridge section of roughly two kilometres with a gradual climb and little shade.

images.alt: Aerial view of the paved Campuhan Ridge Walk between wooded valleys

supports: The route guide describes the ridge as exposed and without shade.

schedulingEligibility.reason: Map-ready walking option close to central Ubud; best treated as a weather-dependent morning activity.

supports: The guide identifies the trailhead beside Pura Gunung Lebah and describes the paved ridge route.

places.name: Tegallalang Rice Terrace

guideDisplay.cardSummary: Steep rice terraces illustrating Bali’s traditional subak irrigation landscape.
guideDisplay.footerNote: Conditions and vegetation vary with weather and the agricultural cycle.

places.whyWorthIt: The valley’s layered paddies make the subak irrigation landscape legible at a glance.
places.plan: Visit earlier in the day and combine with Tirta Empul on one private-driver loop rather than making two separate northbound trips.
places.tip: Expect uneven and potentially muddy paths after rain; the roadside viewpoints are easier than descending deeply into the terraces.

detailSections.title: Cultural context
detailSections.body: Subak is Bali’s traditional cooperative irrigation system, not merely a visual pattern in the landscape.

images.alt: Green terraced rice paddies at Tegallalang near Ubud

supports: The terraces follow Bali’s traditional subak irrigation system.

schedulingEligibility.reason: Map-ready landscape north of Ubud that combines naturally with nearby Tampaksiring stops.

supports: The tourism ministry identifies Tegallalang as a terraced landscape using the traditional subak system.

places.name: Tirta Empul Temple

guideDisplay.cardSummary: Living Balinese Hindu water temple centered on sacred springs and purification pools.
guideDisplay.footerNote: This remains an active place of worship.

places.whyWorthIt: The complex centers on natural springs, historic temple architecture, worship, and the living melukat purification tradition.
places.plan: Visit with a driver and pair it with Tegallalang. Observe worship respectfully; participate in purification only after learning the correct sequence and restrictions from an authorized local guide or temple staff.
places.tip: Wear temple-appropriate clothing and use the required sarong. Two waterspouts are reserved for rites associated with the dead and must not be used by ordinary bathers.

detailSections.title: Sacred use
detailSections.body: Tirta Empul is an active Hindu temple, not a staged bathing attraction.

detailSections.title: Purification pools
detailSections.body: Participation requires local guidance because individual waterspouts have distinct ritual purposes.

images.alt: Sacred bathing pools and water spouts at Tirta Empul Temple

supports: The tourism ministry states that sarongs are used for entry and that two waterspouts are prohibited for living participants.

schedulingEligibility.reason: Map-ready cultural site that fits a private-driver loop from Ubud.

supports: The tourism ministry locates the temple in Manukaya near Tampaksiring and describes its sacred springs.

places.name: Locavore NXT
places.locationLabel: Jalan A.A. Gede Rai, Lodtunduh, Ubud

guideDisplay.cardSummary: Reservation-led tasting menu built around Indonesian ingredients and local sourcing.
guideDisplay.footerNote: This is a high-cost, long-format meal and should replace other evening plans.

places.whyWorthIt: Its set menu explores highly localized Indonesian ingredients through an experimental tasting format.
places.plan: Reserve only after the Ubud lodging dates are fixed. Treat the meal as the evening’s anchor and provide dietary restrictions during booking.
places.tip: Allow a traffic buffer and keep the driver arrangement active; the restaurant is outside central Ubud and provides a driver waiting area.

detailSections.title: Format
detailSections.body: One set tasting menu is offered to a limited number of diners.

detailSections.title: Dietary planning

localFoods.context: Especially relevant around Jimbaran, where seafood and fishing-village traditions shape local menus.

localFoods.title: Regional Indonesian cooking
localFoods.description: A broader food theme spanning Balinese, Javanese, Sumatran, Sulawesian, and other Indonesian traditions.
localFoods.context: Useful for balancing specifically Balinese meals with an introduction to the archipelago’s wider food culture.

localProducts.title: Balinese painting
localProducts.description: Traditional and modern Balinese painting includes distinct Ubud-area schools, techniques, and historical periods.
localProducts.context: Museum visits provide context before considering any art purchase; do not treat museum collections as retail inventory.

localProducts.title: Indonesian handwoven textiles
localProducts.description: Textiles whose fibers, dyes, motifs, maker communities, and island origins form part of the object rather than serving as generic souvenirs.
localProducts.context: Threads of Life is a concrete place to browse these textiles and learn how natural dyes and weaving traditions relate to their communities of origin.

experienceThemes.title: Subak landscapes
experienceThemes.description: Bali’s cooperative irrigation tradition connects water management, agriculture, community, and religious practice.
experienceThemes.context: Tegallalang is the most accessible researched landscape expression of this theme from an Ubud base.

experienceThemes.title: Living temple etiquette
experienceThemes.description: Bali’s temples are active places of worship whose visitor value depends on respectful dress and behavior.
experienceThemes.context: At Tirta Empul, ritual participation requires more care than ordinary sightseeing.

experienceThemes.title: Balinese foodways
experienceThemes.description: Markets, local ingredients, ceremonial dishes, and hands-on cooking reveal how food connects to family and village life.
experienceThemes.context: A cooking class offers more context than adding multiple restaurant meals to the formal itinerary.

experienceThemes.title: Balinese visual and performance arts
experienceThemes.description: Compare painting traditions, masks, puppetry, textiles, and dance as distinct artistic practices rather than treating Ubud culture as one interchangeable category.
experienceThemes.context: The batch adds museum, mask-and-puppet, and textile choices that complement the scheduled Uluwatu Kecak performance and existing Ubud museums.

experienceThemes.title: Pakerisan Valley archaeology
experienceThemes.description: Rock-cut monuments, sacred river landscapes, and hermitage spaces provide historical depth beyond the active water-temple experience at Tirta Empul.
experienceThemes.context: Gunung Kawi is the concrete addable choice, but its stairs and visit duration make it a replacement-level decision rather than casual filler.

experienceThemes.title: Uluwatu coast without a surf commitment
experienceThemes.description: Cliff approaches, beach time, and expert surf scenery can be appreciated without scheduling a surf lesson or entering difficult breaks.
experienceThemes.context: Thomas and Suluban are concrete coastal choices; water entry remains conditional on current official and local safety information.

travelTips.title: Use a driver for cross-island days
travelTips.body: Use a private car or hotel transfer for airport movements, the north-Ubud loop, the hotel change, and Uluwatu. Ride-hailing is better suited to shorter local trips where pickup is permitted.
travelTips.context: This follows the no-motorcycle constraint and avoids relying on unsupported point-to-point duration estimates.

travelTips.title: Keep one indoor Ubud alternative
travelTips.body: October is generally within Bali’s April-to-October dry-season pattern, but seasonal timing is increasingly unpredictable. Preserve ARMA or Museum Puri Lukisan as a same-area substitute for an exposed walk.

travelTips.title: Carry more than one payment method
travelTips.body: Carry a physical card and some Indonesian rupiah for smaller merchants while retaining a backup card. Confirm payment terms when making restaurant reservations.
travelTips.context: Cuca states that it accepts Indonesian-rupiah cash and major cards; policies differ by merchant.

travelTips.title: Protect the international departure buffer
travelTips.body: South Bali traffic can be variable, so the October 12 airport movement should remain the day’s primary execution constraint rather than being preceded by a distant attraction.
travelTips.context: The confirmed flight departs DPS at 17:10.

travelTips.title: Check official coastal warnings
travelTips.body: Before visiting Thomas or Suluban, check current high-wave, strong-current, extreme-weather, and tsunami guidance. Stop coastal activity and follow evacuation or officer instructions when warnings are issued.
travelTips.context: Bali's provincial marine authority says coastal conditions can change quickly and directs the public to official BMKG, maritime, and disaster-management channels.

travelTips.title: Do not treat Uluwatu surf access as casual swimming
travelTips.body: Uluwatu is known for expert surf breaks, including shallow water and strong wave conditions. Use Thomas and Suluban primarily as shore or scenery choices unless current conditions and local guidance support water entry.
travelTips.context: This applies to the added Uluwatu coastal choices and avoids converting a scenic stop into an unsupported swimming plan.

travelTips.title: Follow sacred-site dress and conduct rules
travelTips.body: Wear modest clothing and the required sarong or sash, avoid restricted sacred areas, do not disturb worshippers, and avoid stepping on daily offerings placed along paths.
travelTips.context: Relevant if Gunung Kawi is selected and throughout the existing Bali temple itinerary.

preparationChecklist.title: Obtain or confirm an Indonesian B1 visa on arrival
preparationChecklist.description: For a United States passport holder traveling for tourism, confirm continued B1 eligibility and obtain an e-VoA before travel or a VoA at the arrival checkpoint. The current official rules require a passport valid for at least six months and a return or onward ticket.
preparationChecklist.completionCondition: Each traveler has a valid e-VoA or a documented plan and eligibility to obtain VoA at DPS, with passport validity and onward ticket checked.

preparationChecklist.title: Complete the All Indonesia arrival declaration
preparationChecklist.description: The customs authority directs air and sea arrivals to the All Indonesia system, which integrates immigration, customs, health, and quarantine information and can be completed from three days before arrival.
preparationChecklist.completionCondition: The required declaration is submitted for each applicable traveler and the resulting QR code is saved for arrival.

preparationChecklist.title: Pay the Bali foreign-tourist levy
preparationChecklist.description: The Bali Provincial Government currently requires a Rp150,000 levy per international tourist and encourages online payment before departure. Save the QR-code voucher.
preparationChecklist.completionCondition: A valid levy voucher is stored offline for each non-exempt traveler.

preparationChecklist.title: Select two accommodation bases
preparationChecklist.description: Book one Ubud-area stay followed by one south-Bali stay in Jimbaran, Nusa Dua, or Uluwatu, with only one hotel change. The actual properties determine daily departure points and the transfer plan.
preparationChecklist.completionCondition: Two properties and the single changeover date are confirmed for the Bali nights, with check-in, check-out, and luggage arrangements recorded.

preparationChecklist.title: Arrange airport and long-distance private-car transfers
preparationChecklist.description: Secure a car or driver for DPS to the first hotel, the north-Ubud excursion, the one hotel change, any Uluwatu evening, and the final airport transfer. Do not plan motorcycle rental.
preparationChecklist.completionCondition: Pickup contacts and meeting points are confirmed for both airport movements and any fixed long-distance day.

preparationChecklist.title: Recheck Uluwatu Kecak schedule and ticket channel
preparationChecklist.description: The retrieved operator pages publish a general 18:00–19:00 show and separate ticketing, but do not provide a date-specific October 2026 calendar or live availability.
preparationChecklist.completionCondition: The chosen October 9–11 performance date, start time, authorized ticket channel, and ticket status are confirmed.

preparationChecklist.title: Reserve Locavore NXT if selected
preparationChecklist.description: The restaurant operates limited set-menu seatings and strongly recommends advance booking with a card guarantee and advance disclosure of dietary needs.
preparationChecklist.completionCondition: A table for three is confirmed for a date compatible with the Ubud stay, or the restaurant is left as an unscheduled catalog alternative.

preparationChecklist.title: Book Jala Cooking Academy if selected
preparationChecklist.description: The experience has limited capacity and requires direct confirmation; clarify whether the selected session includes the Jimbaran fish-market component.
preparationChecklist.completionCondition: A class for three, date, start time, inclusions, dietary needs, and cancellation terms are confirmed, or the class remains an Explore alternative.

preparationChecklist.title: Select and reserve the Ubud base
preparationChecklist.description: Choose one Ubud candidate for October 5–9 and confirm occupancy for three travelers, cancellation terms, and arrival transfer arrangements before payment.
preparationChecklist.completionCondition: One Ubud property is reserved for October 5–9 with written occupancy and transfer details.

preparationChecklist.title: Select and reserve the Jimbaran base
preparationChecklist.description: Choose one Jimbaran candidate for October 9–12 and confirm occupancy for three travelers, cancellation terms, and an airport-transfer plan for the October 12 departure.
preparationChecklist.completionCondition: One Jimbaran property is reserved for October 9–12 and the departure-day transfer plan is recorded.

guideRelationships.rationale: Both sit north of Ubud and can share one private-driver outing without duplicating the northbound journey.
Both provide substantial Balinese-art content; selecting one preserves a comfortable pace.
ARMA supplies an indoor cultural option when rain or heat makes the exposed ridge walk unsuitable.
Museum Puri Lukisan is a central-Ubud indoor substitute for an exposed outdoor walk.
The performance is staged at Uluwatu Temple’s open-air venue and naturally follows a late-afternoon temple visit.
Both are in central Ubud and can form a compact museum-and-meal combination.
Cuca is a conventional destination meal, while Jala is a longer hands-on food experience; either can anchor a Jimbaran food day.
ARMA offers a more controlled museum visit if heat, rain, or macaque concerns make the sanctuary less suitable.
These are peer Pecatu coastal choices: Thomas for beach time and Suluban for cliff-cave access and surf scenery.
Kayu Mama provides a bookable low-energy substitute when stairs, surf conditions, or weather make the coastal stop unsuitable.
Peer candidates for the same October 5–9 Ubud base: Maya favors a more secluded garden setting, while Bisma Eight favors central-town access.
Peer beachfront candidates for the same October 9–12 Jimbaran base, with different property scale and atmosphere.

The recommended first base is **Bisma Eight Hotel in Ubud, October 5–9**; its Jalan Bisma location is more convenient than a secluded resort for central Ubud walks, museums, dining, and the Monkey Forest. The recommended second base is **Jimbaran Puri, A Belmond Hotel, October 9–12**, giving the trip a restful beachfront finish, sensible access to Uluwatu, and a practical final route to DPS.\n\nBoth properties are **recommended, not booked**. Confirm room occupancy for three before payment. Maya Ubud Resort & Spa and InterContinental Bali Resort are the researched peer alternatives if room configuration, price, or availability is better, but retain the same dates to preserve the single-change structure.\n\nOctober 3 is preparation, October 4 is long-haul transit, and the Bali stay begins with the stated 10:35 arrival on October 5. Private cars or hotel transfers handle airport movements, the north-Ubud circuit, the hotel change, and Uluwatu. Walking and Grab/Gojek suit short local trips where pickup is permitted. No motorcycle rental is needed.\n\n## Daily itinerary\n\n### Saturday, October 3 — Prepare without rushing\n\n**Start:** Home or pre-flight accommodation in Los Angeles; exact lodging is not supplied.\n\n**Experiences:** Around 10:00, spend 90 minutes checking passports, current Indonesian B1 e-VoA/VoA rules, onward-ticket evidence, the All Indonesia declaration process, and the Bali levy. Around 14:00, finalize the two hotels and request private-transfer arrangements. Pack temple-appropriate clothing, secure shoes, sun and rain protection, medications, and offline copies of essential QR codes. Protect an early night.\n\n**End:** Home or pre-flight accommodation in Los Angeles.\n\n### Sunday, October 4 — Long-haul travel\n\n**Start:** Los Angeles departure airport; the exact airport, terminal, and departure time must come from the airline itinerary.\n\n**Experiences:** Complete international check-in and travel via Singapore. Keep passports, medications, arrival documents, levy records, and the DPS driver contact in carry-on baggage. Prioritize hydration, movement, meals, and sleep; no sightseeing is planned.\n\n**End:** In transit via Singapore to Bali.\n\n### Monday, October 5 — DPS arrival and Ubud adjustment\n\n**Start:** **I Gusti Ngurah Rai International Airport (DPS)** at the stated 10:35 local arrival.\n\n**Experiences:** Allow roughly two hours for immigration, baggage, customs, and levy or declaration checks, recognizing that processing can vary. Meet a pre-arranged private driver around 12:30 and travel directly to Ubud without an en-route attraction. Aim to reach **Bisma Eight Hotel** around 15:00, check in, hydrate, shower, and rest. Have an easy dinner within a short walk or car ride around 18:00, then turn in early.\n\n**End:** **Bisma Eight Hotel — Recommended / Not booked.**\n\n### Tuesday, October 6 — Campuhan, Balinese art, and textiles\n\n**Start:** **Bisma Eight Hotel — Recommended / Not booked.**\n\n**Experiences:** Leave around 07:15 for a 07:45–09:15 **Campuhan Ridge Walk**, using the Pura Gunung Lebah access and choosing an out-and-back distance that suits the group. Recover over breakfast, then visit **Museum Puri Lukisan** from roughly 10:45–12:15 for an introduction to Balinese painting and woodcarving. Lunch at **Hujan Locale** from about 12:30–14:30 provides a substantial seated break and a wider view of regional Indonesian cooking; reserve if the timing matters.\n\nReturn to the hotel for a genuine heat-of-day rest. Around 16:45, visit **Threads of Life Store** for an hour to understand Indonesian weaving, natural dyes, and maker communities, then have dinner in central Ubud and return around 20:15. If rain or heat makes Campuhan unsuitable, replace it with **ARMA**; do not add ARMA on top of the full day.\n\n**End:** **Bisma Eight Hotel — Recommended / Not booked.**\n\n### Wednesday, October 7 — Subak landscape and living temple traditions\n\n**Start:** **Bisma Eight Hotel — Recommended / Not booked.**\n\n**Experiences:** Meet a private driver around 07:30. Visit **Tegallalang Rice Terrace** approximately 08:30–10:00, using the roadside viewpoints if muddy paths or group energy argue against a deep descent. Continue to **Tirta Empul Temple** for about 10:45–12:15. Wear appropriate clothing and observe worship respectfully. Purification is optional and should be attempted only after receiving reliable instruction about the sequence and waterspouts that visitors must not use.\n\nHave lunch in the Tampaksiring or return corridor, then travel back to Ubud around 15:15 for pool or quiet recovery. Keep dinner close to the hotel. **Gunung Kawi** is intentionally not stacked onto this loop: if archaeology is a higher priority and the group is comfortable with substantial stairs, use it instead of Tegallalang.\n\n**End:** **Bisma Eight Hotel — Recommended / Not booked.**\n\n### Thursday, October 8 — Monkey Forest, ARMA, and an optional tasting dinner\n\n**Start:** **Bisma Eight Hotel — Recommended / Not booked.**\n\n**Experiences:** Visit **Sacred Monkey Forest Sanctuary** from about 09:00–11:00. Carry no visible food, keep phones and glasses secure, and do not feed or touch macaques. After lunch and a cooling break, spend approximately 12:45–14:45 at the **Agung Rai Museum of Art**, then return to the hotel to rest and pack gradually for tomorrow.\n\nIf the group wants a destination meal, reserve **Locavore NXT** and leave with a driver around 17:15 for a roughly three-hour tasting dinner. Disclose dietary restrictions and review the card-guarantee terms. If it is unavailable or too formal, have a simple central-Ubud dinner instead; the replacement is preferable to forcing another major attraction into the evening.\n\n**End:** **Bisma Eight Hotel — Recommended / Not booked.**\n\n### Friday, October 9 — The single hotel change\n\n**Start:** **Bisma Eight Hotel — Recommended / Not booked.**\n\n**Experiences:** Have breakfast around 08:00, check out with luggage around 09:30, and depart by private car around 10:00. Travel directly to Jimbaran; traffic makes the approximate three-hour planning window intentionally conservative. Have lunch near Jimbaran Bay, then check in at **Jimbaran Puri** around 14:30. Use the afternoon for beach, pool, or room recovery. Finish with an unhurried Jimbaran seafood dinner, perhaps trying pepes-style seafood, and confirm prices before ordering.\n\nNo sightseeing stop is added en route: luggage, traffic, and the base transition already make this a complete travel day.\n\n**End:** **Jimbaran Puri, A Belmond Hotel — Recommended / Not booked.**\n\n### Saturday, October 10 — Balinese foodways and Jimbaran leisure\n\n**Start:** **Jimbaran Puri, A Belmond Hotel — Recommended / Not booked.**\n\n**Experiences:** After a light breakfast, take hotel transport or a private car to **Jala Cooking Academy** for a provisional 09:30–13:30 session. The class and prepared lunch provide a deeper introduction to Balinese ingredients and techniques than another restaurant-only day. Book for three and confirm the exact session, dietary needs, cancellation terms, and whether a fish-market visit is included.\n\nReturn to the hotel for a long beach, pool, or room recovery block. Around 18:30, share small plates at **Cuca Restaurant**; reserve and review its current table-hold policy. If Jala cannot be booked, turn the morning and early afternoon into a genuine beachfront recovery day rather than adding a distant attraction.\n\n**End:** **Jimbaran Puri, A Belmond Hotel — Recommended / Not booked.**\n\n### Sunday, October 11 — Uluwatu coast, temple, and Kecak\n\n**Start:** **Jimbaran Puri, A Belmond Hotel — Recommended / Not booked.**\n\n**Experiences:** Enjoy a slow breakfast and leave with a retained private driver around 10:00. Spend approximately 11:15–13:15 at **Thomas Beach**, treating it primarily as a scenic, cliff-backed coastal interval. Check official marine warnings and local conditions before any water entry. Have lunch and a shaded rest in Pecatu, then reach **Uluwatu Temple** by about 15:45 for the clifftop paths, sacred setting, admission procedures, and sunset atmosphere. Wear the required sarong or sash and secure loose belongings from macaques.\n\nThe intended evening anchor is the **Uluwatu Kecak and Fire Dance**, provisionally 18:00–19:00. This is not yet a confirmed booking: recheck the October 11 schedule, authorized seller, separate temple and performance tickets, and weather policy. Avoid a tight post-show reservation; return after the crowd clears and have a simple late dinner near or at the hotel. If coastal conditions make Thomas Beach unsuitable, replace it with a pre-booked **Kayu Mama** spa or pool-access product.\n\n**End:** **Jimbaran Puri, A Belmond Hotel — Recommended / Not booked.**\n\n### Monday, October 12 — Protected international departure\n\n**Start:** **Jimbaran Puri, A Belmond Hotel — Recommended / Not booked.**\n\n**Experiences:** Have breakfast and a final quiet beachfront or garden morning without leaving the hotel area. Check out around 10:30, eat an early lunch, and depart for DPS by pre-arranged private car around 12:45. The transfer estimate is deliberately conservative; check traffic and airport guidance on the day. Aim to be at the airport around 13:45 for check-in, baggage, outbound immigration, security, and gate procedures before the stated 17:10 departure via Singapore.\n\nNo distant attraction is scheduled: the flight is the controlling event.\n\n**End:** **I Gusti Ngurah Rai International Airport.**\n\n## Important choices and exclusions\n\n- **Gunung Kawi** is a replacement for Tegallalang, not a third major stop on the north-Ubud loop; its stairs and visit length would make the day rushed.\n- **Neka Art Museum** is omitted because Museum Puri Lukisan and ARMA already provide a balanced art arc. It remains a sensible substitute if either selected museum is unavailable.\n- **Setia Darma House of Masks and Puppets** is worthwhile but would require another vehicle excursion south of Ubud; it loses out to the more compact central plan.\n- **Suluban Beach** is omitted in favor of Thomas Beach, which better supports a relaxed interval before the temple. Neither beach should be treated as guaranteed safe swimming.\n- No attraction is placed on the Ubud–Jimbaran transfer or departure morning because protecting luggage, check-in, and the flight is more valuable than adding another stop.\n\n## Preparation priorities\n\n1. Book the two lodging bases and verify occupancy for three.\n2. Recheck entry authorization, passport, All Indonesia declaration, and Bali levy requirements through official channels.\n3. Arrange the airport transfers, north-Ubud driver, base-change car, and retained Uluwatu driver.\n4. Confirm Jala, Cuca, and optional Locavore reservations.\n5. Recheck and purchase authorized Kecak tickets only after the October 11 session is confirmed.\n6. Refresh opening details, weather, coastal warnings, and route conditions close to each day.\n\nThe supplied research already covered 24 concrete places, four lodging candidates, weather backups, food experiences, and both regional bases. That was sufficient for complete daily experience arcs, so no additional targeted research was necessary."}

parsedInitialPlan.tripStrategy: Use two bases and only one hotel change: four nights at Bisma Eight Hotel in Ubud (recommended, not booked) from October 5–9, followed by three nights at Jimbaran Puri, A Belmond Hotel (recommended, not booked) from October 9–12. Bisma Eight is preferred over the more secluded Maya Ubud because its central location reduces friction for the Monkey Forest, Campuhan Ridge, museums, textiles, and dining; a private driver handles the north-Ubud loop. Jimbaran provides a restful beachfront finish, practical access to Uluwatu, and a shorter departure-day route to DPS. October 3–4 are treated as pre-departure and long-haul travel days because the confirmed local arrival is October 5. The pace alternates substantial cultural days with lower-energy coastal time, protects arrival and departure, and avoids motorcycles. All lodging and activity reservations remain unbooked unless subsequently confirmed.

# Bali: Ubud and Jimbaran

**October 3–12, 2026 · 3 travelers · relaxed cultural and coastal journey**

## Trip strategy

Use two bases with one hotel change. The recommended first base is **Bisma Eight Hotel in Ubud, October 5–9**; its Jalan Bisma location is more convenient than a secluded resort for central Ubud walks, museums, dining, and the Monkey Forest. The recommended second base is **Jimbaran Puri, A Belmond Hotel, October 9–12**, giving the trip a restful beachfront finish, sensible access to Uluwatu, and a practical final route to DPS.

Both properties are **recommended, not booked**. Confirm room occupancy for three before payment. Maya Ubud Resort & Spa and InterContinental Bali Resort are the researched peer alternatives if room configuration, price, or availability is better, but retain the same dates to preserve the single-change structure.

October 3 is preparation, October 4 is long-haul transit, and the Bali stay begins with the stated 10:35 arrival on October 5. Private cars or hotel transfers handle airport movements, the north-Ubud circuit, the hotel change, and Uluwatu. Walking and Grab/Gojek suit short local trips where pickup is permitted. No motorcycle rental is needed.

## Daily itinerary

### Saturday, October 3 — Prepare without rushing

**Start:** Home or pre-flight accommodation in Los Angeles; exact lodging is not supplied.

**Experiences:** Around 10:00, spend 90 minutes checking passports, current Indonesian B1 e-VoA/VoA rules, onward-ticket evidence, the All Indonesia declaration process, and the Bali levy. Around 14:00, finalize the two hotels and request private-transfer arrangements. Pack temple-appropriate clothing, secure shoes, sun and rain protection, medications, and offline copies of essential QR codes. Protect an early night.

**End:** Home or pre-flight accommodation in Los Angeles.

### Sunday, October 4 — Long-haul travel

**Start:** Los Angeles departure airport; the exact airport, terminal, and departure time must come from the airline itinerary.

**Experiences:** Complete international check-in and travel via Singapore. Keep passports, medications, arrival documents, levy records, and the DPS driver contact in carry-on baggage. Prioritize hydration, movement, meals, and sleep; no sightseeing is planned.

**End:** In transit via Singapore to Bali.

### Monday, October 5 — DPS arrival and Ubud adjustment

**Start:** **I Gusti Ngurah Rai International Airport (DPS)** at the stated 10:35 local arrival.

**Experiences:** Allow roughly two hours for immigration, baggage, customs, and levy or declaration checks, recognizing that processing can vary. Meet a pre-arranged private driver around 12:30 and travel directly to Ubud without an en-route attraction. Aim to reach **Bisma Eight Hotel** around 15:00, check in, hydrate, shower, and rest. Have an easy dinner within a short walk or car ride around 18:00, then turn in early.

**End:** **Bisma Eight Hotel — Recommended / Not booked.**

### Tuesday, October 6 — Campuhan, Balinese art, and textiles

**Start:** **Bisma Eight Hotel — Recommended / Not booked.**

**Experiences:** Leave around 07:15 for a 07:45–09:15 **Campuhan Ridge Walk**, using the Pura Gunung Lebah access and choosing an out-and-back distance that suits the group. Recover over breakfast, then visit **Museum Puri Lukisan** from roughly 10:45–12:15 for an introduction to Balinese painting and woodcarving. Lunch at **Hujan Locale** from about 12:30–14:30 provides a substantial seated break and a wider view of regional Indonesian cooking; reserve if the timing matters.

Return to the hotel for a genuine heat-of-day rest. Around 16:45, visit **Threads of Life Store** for an hour to understand Indonesian weaving, natural dyes, and maker communities, then have dinner in central Ubud and return around 20:15. If rain or heat makes Campuhan unsuitable, replace it with **ARMA**; do not add ARMA on top of the full day.

**End:** **Bisma Eight Hotel — Recommended / Not booked.**

### Wednesday, October 7 — Subak landscape and living temple traditions

**Start:** **Bisma Eight Hotel — Recommended / Not booked.**

**Experiences:** Meet a private driver around 07:30. Visit **Tegallalang Rice Terrace** approximately 08:30–10:00, using the roadside viewpoints if muddy paths or group energy argue against a deep descent. Continue to **Tirta Empul Temple** for about 10:45–12:15. Wear appropriate clothing and observe worship respectfully. Purification is optional and should be attempted only after receiving reliable instruction about the sequence and waterspouts that visitors must not use.

Have lunch in the Tampaksiring or return corridor, then travel back to Ubud around 15:15 for pool or quiet recovery. Keep dinner close to the hotel. **Gunung Kawi** is intentionally not stacked onto this loop: if archaeology is a higher priority and the group is comfortable with substantial stairs, use it instead of Tegallalang.

**End:** **Bisma Eight Hotel — Recommended / Not booked.**

### Thursday, October 8 — Monkey Forest, ARMA, and an optional tasting dinner

**Start:** **Bisma Eight Hotel — Recommended / Not booked.**

**Experiences:** Visit **Sacred Monkey Forest Sanctuary** from about 09:00–11:00. Carry no visible food, keep phones and glasses secure, and do not feed or touch macaques. After lunch and a cooling break, spend approximately 12:45–14:45 at the **Agung Rai Museum of Art**, then return to the hotel to rest and pack gradually for tomorrow.

If the group wants a destination meal, reserve **Locavore NXT** and leave with a driver around 17:15 for a roughly three-hour tasting dinner. Disclose dietary restrictions and review the card-guarantee terms. If it is unavailable or too formal, have a simple central-Ubud dinner instead; the replacement is preferable to forcing another major attraction into the evening.

**End:** **Bisma Eight Hotel — Recommended / Not booked.**

### Friday, October 9 — The single hotel change

**Start:** **Bisma Eight Hotel — Recommended / Not booked.**

**Experiences:** Have breakfast around 08:00, check out with luggage around 09:30, and depart by private car around 10:00. Travel directly to Jimbaran; traffic makes the approximate three-hour planning window intentionally conservative. Have lunch near Jimbaran Bay, then check in at **Jimbaran Puri** around 14:30. Use the afternoon for beach, pool, or room recovery. Finish with an unhurried Jimbaran seafood dinner, perhaps trying pepes-style seafood, and confirm prices before ordering.

No sightseeing stop is added en route: luggage, traffic, and the base transition already make this a complete travel day.

**End:** **Jimbaran Puri, A Belmond Hotel — Recommended / Not booked.**

### Saturday, October 10 — Balinese foodways and Jimbaran leisure

**Start:** **Jimbaran Puri, A Belmond Hotel — Recommended / Not booked.**

**Experiences:** After a light breakfast, take hotel transport or a private car to **Jala Cooking Academy** for a provisional 09:30–13:30 session. The class and prepared lunch provide a deeper introduction to Balinese ingredients and techniques than another restaurant-only day. Book for three and confirm the exact session, dietary needs, cancellation terms, and whether a fish-market visit is included.

Return to the hotel for a long beach, pool, or room recovery block. Around 18:30, share small plates at **Cuca Restaurant**; reserve and review its current table-hold policy. If Jala cannot be booked, turn the morning and early afternoon into a genuine beachfront recovery day rather than adding a distant attraction.

**End:** **Jimbaran Puri, A Belmond Hotel — Recommended / Not booked.**

### Sunday, October 11 — Uluwatu coast, temple, and Kecak

**Start:** **Jimbaran Puri, A Belmond Hotel — Recommended / Not booked.**

**Experiences:** Enjoy a slow breakfast and leave with a retained private driver around 10:00. Spend approximately 11:15–13:15 at **Thomas Beach**, treating it primarily as a scenic, cliff-backed coastal interval. Check official marine warnings and local conditions before any water entry. Have lunch and a shaded rest in Pecatu, then reach **Uluwatu Temple** by about 15:45 for the clifftop paths, sacred setting, admission procedures, and sunset atmosphere. Wear the required sarong or sash and secure loose belongings from macaques.

The intended evening anchor is the **Uluwatu Kecak and Fire Dance**, provisionally 18:00–19:00. This is not yet a confirmed booking: recheck the October 11 schedule, authorized seller, separate temple and performance tickets, and weather policy. Avoid a tight post-show reservation; return after the crowd clears and have a simple late dinner near or at the hotel. If coastal conditions make Thomas Beach unsuitable, replace it with a pre-booked **Kayu Mama** spa or pool-access product.

**End:** **Jimbaran Puri, A Belmond Hotel — Recommended / Not booked.**

### Monday, October 12 — Protected international departure

**Start:** **Jimbaran Puri, A Belmond Hotel — Recommended / Not booked.**

**Experiences:** Have breakfast and a final quiet beachfront or garden morning without leaving the hotel area. Check out around 10:30, eat an early lunch, and depart for DPS by pre-arranged private car around 12:45. The transfer estimate is deliberately conservative; check traffic and airport guidance on the day. Aim to be at the airport around 13:45 for check-in, baggage, outbound immigration, security, and gate procedures before the stated 17:10 departure via Singapore.

No distant attraction is scheduled: the flight is the controlling event.

**End:** **I Gusti Ngurah Rai International Airport.**

## Important choices and exclusions

- **Gunung Kawi** is a replacement for Tegallalang, not a third major stop on the north-Ubud loop; its stairs and visit length would make the day rushed.
- **Neka Art Museum** is omitted because Museum Puri Lukisan and ARMA already provide a balanced art arc. It remains a sensible substitute if either selected museum is unavailable.
- **Setia Darma House of Masks and Puppets** is worthwhile but would require another vehicle excursion south of Ubud; it loses out to the more compact central plan.
- **Suluban Beach** is omitted in favor of Thomas Beach, which better supports a relaxed interval before the temple. Neither beach should be treated as guaranteed safe swimming.
- No attraction is placed on the Ubud–Jimbaran transfer or departure morning because protecting luggage, check-in, and the flight is more valuable than adding another stop.

## Preparation priorities

1. Book the two lodging bases and verify occupancy for three.
2. Recheck entry authorization, passport, All Indonesia declaration, and Bali levy requirements through official channels.
3. Arrange the airport transfers, north-Ubud driver, base-change car, and retained Uluwatu driver.
4. Confirm Jala, Cuca, and optional Locavore reservations.
5. Recheck and purchase authorized Kecak tickets only after the October 11 session is confirmed.
6. Refresh opening details, weather, coastal warnings, and route conditions close to each day.

The supplied research already covered 24 concrete places, four lodging candidates, weather backups, food experiences, and both regional bases. That was sufficient for complete daily experience arcs, so no additional targeted research was necessary.

# Bali: Ubud and Jimbaran

**October 3–12, 2026 · 3 travelers · relaxed cultural and coastal journey**

## Trip strategy

Use two bases with one hotel change. The recommended first base is **Bisma Eight Hotel in Ubud, October 5–9**; its Jalan Bisma location is more convenient than a secluded resort for central Ubud walks, museums, dining, and the Monkey Forest. The recommended second base is **Jimbaran Puri, A Belmond Hotel, October 9–12**, giving the trip a restful beachfront finish, sensible access to Uluwatu, and a practical final route to DPS.

Both properties are **recommended, not booked**. Confirm room occupancy for three before payment. Maya Ubud Resort & Spa and InterContinental Bali Resort are the researched peer alternatives if room configuration, price, or availability is better, but retain the same dates to preserve the single-change structure.

October 3 is preparation, October 4 is long-haul transit, and the Bali stay begins with the stated 10:35 arrival on October 5. Private cars or hotel transfers handle airport movements, the north-Ubud circuit, the hotel change, and Uluwatu. Walking and Grab/Gojek suit short local trips where pickup is permitted. No motorcycle rental is needed.

## Daily itinerary

### Saturday, October 3 — Prepare without rushing

**Start:** Home or pre-flight accommodation in Los Angeles; exact lodging is not supplied.

**Experiences:** Around 10:00, spend 90 minutes checking passports, current Indonesian B1 e-VoA/VoA rules, onward-ticket evidence, the All Indonesia declaration process, and the Bali levy. Around 14:00, finalize the two hotels and request private-transfer arrangements. Pack temple-appropriate clothing, secure shoes, sun and rain protection, medications, and offline copies of essential QR codes. Protect an early night.

**End:** Home or pre-flight accommodation in Los Angeles.

### Sunday, October 4 — Long-haul travel

**Start:** Los Angeles departure airport; the exact airport, terminal, and departure time must come from the airline itinerary.

**Experiences:** Complete international check-in and travel via Singapore. Keep passports, medications, arrival documents, levy records, and the DPS driver contact in carry-on baggage. Prioritize hydration, movement, meals, and sleep; no sightseeing is planned.

**End:** In transit via Singapore to Bali.

### Monday, October 5 — DPS arrival and Ubud adjustment

**Start:** **I Gusti Ngurah Rai International Airport (DPS)** at the stated 10:35 local arrival.

**Experiences:** Allow roughly two hours for immigration, baggage, customs, and levy or declaration checks, recognizing that processing can vary. Meet a pre-arranged private driver around 12:30 and travel directly to Ubud without an en-route attraction. Aim to reach **Bisma Eight Hotel** around 15:00, check in, hydrate, shower, and rest. Have an easy dinner within a short walk or car ride around 18:00, then turn in early.

**End:** **Bisma Eight Hotel — Recommended / Not booked.**

### Tuesday, October 6 — Campuhan, Balinese art, and textiles

**Start:** **Bisma Eight Hotel — Recommended / Not booked.**

**Experiences:** Leave around 07:15 for a 07:45–09:15 **Campuhan Ridge Walk**, using the Pura Gunung Lebah access and choosing an out-and-back distance that suits the group. Recover over breakfast, then visit **Museum Puri Lukisan** from roughly 10:45–12:15 for an introduction to Balinese painting and woodcarving. Lunch at **Hujan Locale** from about 12:30–14:30 provides a substantial seated break and a wider view of regional Indonesian cooking; reserve if the timing matters.

Return to the hotel for a genuine heat-of-day rest. Around 16:45, visit **Threads of Life Store** for an hour to understand Indonesian weaving, natural dyes, and maker communities, then have dinner in central Ubud and return around 20:15. If rain or heat makes Campuhan unsuitable, replace it with **ARMA**; do not add ARMA on top of the full day.

**End:** **Bisma Eight Hotel — Recommended / Not booked.**

### Wednesday, October 7 — Subak landscape and living temple traditions

**Start:** **Bisma Eight Hotel — Recommended / Not booked.**

**Experiences:** Meet a private driver around 07:30. Visit **Tegallalang Rice Terrace** approximately 08:30–10:00, using the roadside viewpoints if muddy paths or group energy argue against a deep descent. Continue to **Tirta Empul Temple** for about 10:45–12:15. Wear appropriate clothing and observe worship respectfully. Purification is optional and should be attempted only after receiving reliable instruction about the sequence and waterspouts that visitors must not use.

Have lunch in the Tampaksiring or return corridor, then travel back to Ubud around 15:15 for pool or quiet recovery. Keep dinner close to the hotel. **Gunung Kawi** is intentionally not stacked onto this loop: if archaeology is a higher priority and the group is comfortable with substantial stairs, use it instead of Tegallalang.

**End:** **Bisma Eight Hotel — Recommended / Not booked.**

### Thursday, October 8 — Monkey Forest, ARMA, and an optional tasting dinner

**Start:** **Bisma Eight Hotel — Recommended / Not booked.**

**Experiences:** Visit **Sacred Monkey Forest Sanctuary** from about 09:00–11:00. Carry no visible food, keep phones and glasses secure, and do not feed or touch macaques. After lunch and a cooling break, spend approximately 12:45–14:45 at the **Agung Rai Museum of Art**, then return to the hotel to rest and pack gradually for tomorrow.

If the group wants a destination meal, reserve **Locavore NXT** and leave with a driver around 17:15 for a roughly three-hour tasting dinner. Disclose dietary restrictions and review the card-guarantee terms. If it is unavailable or too formal, have a simple central-Ubud dinner instead; the replacement is preferable to forcing another major attraction into the evening.

**End:** **Bisma Eight Hotel — Recommended / Not booked.**

### Friday, October 9 — The single hotel change

**Start:** **Bisma Eight Hotel — Recommended / Not booked.**

**Experiences:** Have breakfast around 08:00, check out with luggage around 09:30, and depart by private car around 10:00. Travel directly to Jimbaran; traffic makes the approximate three-hour planning window intentionally conservative. Have lunch near Jimbaran Bay, then check in at **Jimbaran Puri** around 14:30. Use the afternoon for beach, pool, or room recovery. Finish with an unhurried Jimbaran seafood dinner, perhaps trying pepes-style seafood, and confirm prices before ordering.

No sightseeing stop is added en route: luggage, traffic, and the base transition already make this a complete travel day.

**End:** **Jimbaran Puri, A Belmond Hotel — Recommended / Not booked.**

### Saturday, October 10 — Balinese foodways and Jimbaran leisure

**Start:** **Jimbaran Puri, A Belmond Hotel — Recommended / Not booked.**

**Experiences:** After a light breakfast, take hotel transport or a private car to **Jala Cooking Academy** for a provisional 09:30–13:30 session. The class and prepared lunch provide a deeper introduction to Balinese ingredients and techniques than another restaurant-only day. Book for three and confirm the exact session, dietary needs, cancellation terms, and whether a fish-market visit is included.

Return to the hotel for a long beach, pool, or room recovery block. Around 18:30, share small plates at **Cuca Restaurant**; reserve and review its current table-hold policy. If Jala cannot be booked, turn the morning and early afternoon into a genuine beachfront recovery day rather than adding a distant attraction.

**End:** **Jimbaran Puri, A Belmond Hotel — Recommended / Not booked.**

### Sunday, October 11 — Uluwatu coast, temple, and Kecak

**Start:** **Jimbaran Puri, A Belmond Hotel — Recommended / Not booked.**

**Experiences:** Enjoy a slow breakfast and leave with a retained private driver around 10:00. Spend approximately 11:15–13:15 at **Thomas Beach**, treating it primarily as a scenic, cliff-backed coastal interval. Check official marine warnings and local conditions before any water entry. Have lunch and a shaded rest in Pecatu, then reach **Uluwatu Temple** by about 15:45 for the clifftop paths, sacred setting, admission procedures, and sunset atmosphere. Wear the required sarong or sash and secure loose belongings from macaques.

The intended evening anchor is the **Uluwatu Kecak and Fire Dance**, provisionally 18:00–19:00. This is not yet a confirmed booking: recheck the October 11 schedule, authorized seller, separate temple and performance tickets, and weather policy. Avoid a tight post-show reservation; return after the crowd clears and have a simple late dinner near or at the hotel. If coastal conditions make Thomas Beach unsuitable, replace it with a pre-booked **Kayu Mama** spa or pool-access product.

**End:** **Jimbaran Puri, A Belmond Hotel — Recommended / Not booked.**

### Monday, October 12 — Protected international departure

**Start:** **Jimbaran Puri, A Belmond Hotel — Recommended / Not booked.**

**Experiences:** Have breakfast and a final quiet beachfront or garden morning without leaving the hotel area. Check out around 10:30, eat an early lunch, and depart for DPS by pre-arranged private car around 12:45. The transfer estimate is deliberately conservative; check traffic and airport guidance on the day. Aim to be at the airport around 13:45 for check-in, baggage, outbound immigration, security, and gate procedures before the stated 17:10 departure via Singapore.

No distant attraction is scheduled: the flight is the controlling event.

**End:** **I Gusti Ngurah Rai International Airport.**

## Important choices and exclusions

- **Gunung Kawi** is a replacement for Tegallalang, not a third major stop on the north-Ubud loop; its stairs and visit length would make the day rushed.
- **Neka Art Museum** is omitted because Museum Puri Lukisan and ARMA already provide a balanced art arc. It remains a sensible substitute if either selected museum is unavailable.
- **Setia Darma House of Masks and Puppets** is worthwhile but would require another vehicle excursion south of Ubud; it loses out to the more compact central plan.
- **Suluban Beach** is omitted in favor of Thomas Beach, which better supports a relaxed interval before the temple. Neither beach should be treated as guaranteed safe swimming.
- No attraction is placed on the Ubud–Jimbaran transfer or departure morning because protecting luggage, check-in, and the flight is more valuable than adding another stop.

## Preparation priorities

1. Book the two lodging bases and verify occupancy for three.
2. Recheck entry authorization, passport, All Indonesia declaration, and Bali levy requirements through official channels.
3. Arrange the airport transfers, north-Ubud driver, base-change car, and retained Uluwatu driver.
4. Confirm Jala, Cuca, and optional Locavore reservations.
5. Recheck and purchase authorized Kecak tickets only after the October 11 session is confirmed.
6. Refresh opening details, weather, coastal warnings, and route conditions close to each day.

The supplied research already covered 24 concrete places, four lodging candidates, weather backups, food experiences, and both regional bases. That was sufficient for complete daily experience arcs, so no additional targeted research was necessary.

semanticPlan.title: Bali, Indonesia — Ubud and Jimbaran Leisure Journey
semanticPlan.tripStrategy: Use two bases and only one hotel change: four nights at Bisma Eight Hotel in Ubud (recommended, not booked) from October 5–9, followed by three nights at Jimbaran Puri, A Belmond Hotel (recommended, not booked) from October 9–12. Bisma Eight is preferred over the more secluded Maya Ubud because its central location reduces friction for the Monkey Forest, Campuhan Ridge, museums, textiles, and dining; a private driver handles the north-Ubud loop. Jimbaran provides a restful beachfront finish, practical access to Uluwatu, and a shorter departure-day route to DPS. October 3–4 are treated as pre-departure and long-haul travel days because the confirmed local arrival is October 5. The pace alternates substantial cultural days with lower-energy coastal time, protects arrival and departure, and avoids motorcycles. All lodging and activity reservations remain unbooked unless subsequently confirmed.

# Bali: Ubud and Jimbaran

**October 3–12, 2026 · 3 travelers · relaxed cultural and coastal journey**

## Trip strategy

Use two bases with one hotel change. The recommended first base is **Bisma Eight Hotel in Ubud, October 5–9**; its Jalan Bisma location is more convenient than a secluded resort for central Ubud walks, museums, dining, and the Monkey Forest. The recommended second base is **Jimbaran Puri, A Belmond Hotel, October 9–12**, giving the trip a restful beachfront finish, sensible access to Uluwatu, and a practical final route to DPS.

Both properties are **recommended, not booked**. Confirm room occupancy for three before payment. Maya Ubud Resort & Spa and InterContinental Bali Resort are the researched peer alternatives if room configuration, price, or availability is better, but retain the same dates to preserve the single-change structure.

October 3 is preparation, October 4 is long-haul transit, and the Bali stay begins with the stated 10:35 arrival on October 5. Private cars or hotel transfers handle airport movements, the north-Ubud circuit, the hotel change, and Uluwatu. Walking and Grab/Gojek suit short local trips where pickup is permitted. No motorcycle rental is needed.

## Daily itinerary

### Saturday, October 3 — Prepare without rushing

**Start:** Home or pre-flight accommodation in Los Angeles; exact lodging is not supplied.

**Experiences:** Around 10:00, spend 90 minutes checking passports, current Indonesian B1 e-VoA/VoA rules, onward-ticket evidence, the All Indonesia declaration process, and the Bali levy. Around 14:00, finalize the two hotels and request private-transfer arrangements. Pack temple-appropriate clothing, secure shoes, sun and rain protection, medications, and offline copies of essential QR codes. Protect an early night.

**End:** Home or pre-flight accommodation in Los Angeles.

### Sunday, October 4 — Long-haul travel

**Start:** Los Angeles departure airport; the exact airport, terminal, and departure time must come from the airline itinerary.

**Experiences:** Complete international check-in and travel via Singapore. Keep passports, medications, arrival documents, levy records, and the DPS driver contact in carry-on baggage. Prioritize hydration, movement, meals, and sleep; no sightseeing is planned.

**End:** In transit via Singapore to Bali.

### Monday, October 5 — DPS arrival and Ubud adjustment

**Start:** **I Gusti Ngurah Rai International Airport (DPS)** at the stated 10:35 local arrival.

**Experiences:** Allow roughly two hours for immigration, baggage, customs, and levy or declaration checks, recognizing that processing can vary. Meet a pre-arranged private driver around 12:30 and travel directly to Ubud without an en-route attraction. Aim to reach **Bisma Eight Hotel** around 15:00, check in, hydrate, shower, and rest. Have an easy dinner within a short walk or car ride around 18:00, then turn in early.

**End:** **Bisma Eight Hotel — Recommended / Not booked.**

### Tuesday, October 6 — Campuhan, Balinese art, and textiles

**Start:** **Bisma Eight Hotel — Recommended / Not booked.**

**Experiences:** Leave around 07:15 for a 07:45–09:15 **Campuhan Ridge Walk**, using the Pura Gunung Lebah access and choosing an out-and-back distance that suits the group. Recover over breakfast, then visit **Museum Puri Lukisan** from roughly 10:45–12:15 for an introduction to Balinese painting and woodcarving. Lunch at **Hujan Locale** from about 12:30–14:30 provides a substantial seated break and a wider view of regional Indonesian cooking; reserve if the timing matters.

Return to the hotel for a genuine heat-of-day rest. Around 16:45, visit **Threads of Life Store** for an hour to understand Indonesian weaving, natural dyes, and maker communities, then have dinner in central Ubud and return around 20:15. If rain or heat makes Campuhan unsuitable, replace it with **ARMA**; do not add ARMA on top of the full day.

**End:** **Bisma Eight Hotel — Recommended / Not booked.**

### Wednesday, October 7 — Subak landscape and living temple traditions

**Start:** **Bisma Eight Hotel — Recommended / Not booked.**

**Experiences:** Meet a private driver around 07:30. Visit **Tegallalang Rice Terrace** approximately 08:30–10:00, using the roadside viewpoints if muddy paths or group energy argue against a deep descent. Continue to **Tirta Empul Temple** for about 10:45–12:15. Wear appropriate clothing and observe worship respectfully. Purification is optional and should be attempted only after receiving reliable instruction about the sequence and waterspouts that visitors must not use.

Have lunch in the Tampaksiring or return corridor, then travel back to Ubud around 15:15 for pool or quiet recovery. Keep dinner close to the hotel. **Gunung Kawi** is intentionally not stacked onto this loop: if archaeology is a higher priority and the group is comfortable with substantial stairs, use it instead of Tegallalang.

**End:** **Bisma Eight Hotel — Recommended / Not booked.**

### Thursday, October 8 — Monkey Forest, ARMA, and an optional tasting dinner

**Start:** **Bisma Eight Hotel — Recommended / Not booked.**

**Experiences:** Visit **Sacred Monkey Forest Sanctuary** from about 09:00–11:00. Carry no visible food, keep phones and glasses secure, and do not feed or touch macaques. After lunch and a cooling break, spend approximately 12:45–14:45 at the **Agung Rai Museum of Art**, then return to the hotel to rest and pack gradually for tomorrow.

If the group wants a destination meal, reserve **Locavore NXT** and leave with a driver around 17:15 for a roughly three-hour tasting dinner. Disclose dietary restrictions and review the card-guarantee terms. If it is unavailable or too formal, have a simple central-Ubud dinner instead; the replacement is preferable to forcing another major attraction into the evening.

**End:** **Bisma Eight Hotel — Recommended / Not booked.**

### Friday, October 9 — The single hotel change

**Start:** **Bisma Eight Hotel — Recommended / Not booked.**

**Experiences:** Have breakfast around 08:00, check out with luggage around 09:30, and depart by private car around 10:00. Travel directly to Jimbaran; traffic makes the approximate three-hour planning window intentionally conservative. Have lunch near Jimbaran Bay, then check in at **Jimbaran Puri** around 14:30. Use the afternoon for beach, pool, or room recovery. Finish with an unhurried Jimbaran seafood dinner, perhaps trying pepes-style seafood, and confirm prices before ordering.

No sightseeing stop is added en route: luggage, traffic, and the base transition already make this a complete travel day.

**End:** **Jimbaran Puri, A Belmond Hotel — Recommended / Not booked.**

### Saturday, October 10 — Balinese foodways and Jimbaran leisure

**Start:** **Jimbaran Puri, A Belmond Hotel — Recommended / Not booked.**

**Experiences:** After a light breakfast, take hotel transport or a private car to **Jala Cooking Academy** for a provisional 09:30–13:30 session. The class and prepared lunch provide a deeper introduction to Balinese ingredients and techniques than another restaurant-only day. Book for three and confirm the exact session, dietary needs, cancellation terms, and whether a fish-market visit is included.

Return to the hotel for a long beach, pool, or room recovery block. Around 18:30, share small plates at **Cuca Restaurant**; reserve and review its current table-hold policy. If Jala cannot be booked, turn the morning and early afternoon into a genuine beachfront recovery day rather than adding a distant attraction.

**End:** **Jimbaran Puri, A Belmond Hotel — Recommended / Not booked.**

### Sunday, October 11 — Uluwatu coast, temple, and Kecak

**Start:** **Jimbaran Puri, A Belmond Hotel — Recommended / Not booked.**

**Experiences:** Enjoy a slow breakfast and leave with a retained private driver around 10:00. Spend approximately 11:15–13:15 at **Thomas Beach**, treating it primarily as a scenic, cliff-backed coastal interval. Check official marine warnings and local conditions before any water entry. Have lunch and a shaded rest in Pecatu, then reach **Uluwatu Temple** by about 15:45 for the clifftop paths, sacred setting, admission procedures, and sunset atmosphere. Wear the required sarong or sash and secure loose belongings from macaques.

The intended evening anchor is the **Uluwatu Kecak and Fire Dance**, provisionally 18:00–19:00. This is not yet a confirmed booking: recheck the October 11 schedule, authorized seller, separate temple and performance tickets, and weather policy. Avoid a tight post-show reservation; return after the crowd clears and have a simple late dinner near or at the hotel. If coastal conditions make Thomas Beach unsuitable, replace it with a pre-booked **Kayu Mama** spa or pool-access product.

**End:** **Jimbaran Puri, A Belmond Hotel — Recommended / Not booked.**

### Monday, October 12 — Protected international departure

**Start:** **Jimbaran Puri, A Belmond Hotel — Recommended / Not booked.**

**Experiences:** Have breakfast and a final quiet beachfront or garden morning without leaving the hotel area. Check out around 10:30, eat an early lunch, and depart for DPS by pre-arranged private car around 12:45. The transfer estimate is deliberately conservative; check traffic and airport guidance on the day. Aim to be at the airport around 13:45 for check-in, baggage, outbound immigration, security, and gate procedures before the stated 17:10 departure via Singapore.

No distant attraction is scheduled: the flight is the controlling event.

**End:** **I Gusti Ngurah Rai International Airport.**

## Important choices and exclusions

- **Gunung Kawi** is a replacement for Tegallalang, not a third major stop on the north-Ubud loop; its stairs and visit length would make the day rushed.
- **Neka Art Museum** is omitted because Museum Puri Lukisan and ARMA already provide a balanced art arc. It remains a sensible substitute if either selected museum is unavailable.
- **Setia Darma House of Masks and Puppets** is worthwhile but would require another vehicle excursion south of Ubud; it loses out to the more compact central plan.
- **Suluban Beach** is omitted in favor of Thomas Beach, which better supports a relaxed interval before the temple. Neither beach should be treated as guaranteed safe swimming.
- No attraction is placed on the Ubud–Jimbaran transfer or departure morning because protecting luggage, check-in, and the flight is more valuable than adding another stop.

## Preparation priorities

1. Book the two lodging bases and verify occupancy for three.
2. Recheck entry authorization, passport, All Indonesia declaration, and Bali levy requirements through official channels.
3. Arrange the airport transfers, north-Ubud driver, base-change car, and retained Uluwatu driver.
4. Confirm Jala, Cuca, and optional Locavore reservations.
5. Recheck and purchase authorized Kecak tickets only after the October 11 session is confirmed.
6. Refresh opening details, weather, coastal warnings, and route conditions close to each day.

The supplied research already covered 24 concrete places, four lodging candidates, weather backups, food experiences, and both regional bases. That was sufficient for complete daily experience arcs, so no additional targeted research was necessary.

researchGrounding: The supplied ResearchSet contains 24 concrete places across both proposed bases, including four accommodation candidates and sufficiently varied cultural, landscape, food, beach, wellness, and weather-backup options. No supplemental research was needed to construct complete, geographically coherent days.

The base strategy uses the researched accommodation windows directly: Ubud from October 5–9 and Jimbaran from October 9–12. Bisma Eight was selected for walkable central-Ubud access; Jimbaran Puri was selected for its bay setting and practical relationship to DPS.

Ubud planning is grounded in official or identified sources for Sacred Monkey Forest Sanctuary, Museum Puri Lukisan, ARMA, Tegallalang Rice Terrace, Tirta Empul, Hujan Locale, and Locavore NXT, plus supplied research for Campuhan Ridge and Threads of Life.

The north-Ubud day deliberately excludes Gunung Kawi from the primary plan because its stairs and 150-minute visit would compress Tegallalang and Tirta Empul. It remains a replacement for Tegallalang, not an add-on.

South-Bali planning is grounded in the supplied Uluwatu Temple and Kecak research, Jala Cooking Academy, Cuca, Thomas Beach, Kayu Mama, official coastal-safety guidance, and the two Jimbaran accommodation candidates.

Neka Art Museum, Setia Darma House of Masks and Puppets, and Suluban Beach are intentionally not scheduled: Neka would repeat the selected art museums, Setia Darma would add a separate south-of-Ubud vehicle excursion, and Suluban’s stairs and surf-access character add less relaxed value than Thomas Beach for this party.
